title: karma: the Bhagavata's Uddhava Gita
hook: after the whole long teaching, Uddhava says it's too hard, and Krishna's answer is short and gentle

segments.voice: Yesterday's karma lesson sorted the worker: free, driven, fogged, or beyond the strands. Which worker showed up for your ordinary task? Day one thousand two hundred seven.
screen: `FREE, DRIVEN, OR FOGGED.` · `THE CLOSE OF THE DIALOGUE.`

segments.voice: After all of it, the earth, the three paths, the beggar's song, the strands, Uddhava says something brave. Near the close of the dialogue he tells Krishna that the yoga he's described is hard for anyone who can't master the mind. Hard, he says in effect, for people like us. Give us something a person can actually do. It's the student raising a hand at the end of a long lecture to say: I didn't get all that. And Krishna doesn't sigh or start over. His answer is short, and surprisingly gentle.
screen: `THIS IS TOO HARD.` → `GIVE US SOMETHING DOABLE.` → `A SHORT, GENTLE ANSWER.`

segments.voice: Krishna's answer, in paraphrase: do all your work for my sake, remembering me, slowly, little by little. That's it. No new technique. The work stays the same: the cooking, the trading, the caring for children and parents. What changes is who it's for. Then he widens it. See me in every being, he says, inside them and outside them, the way the sky is in everything. And then a line that asks a great deal: bow down to everyone, even to a dog, a donkey, a cow, even to the person your society pushes to the edges, and don't mind if your own people laugh at you. The text names the creatures and people its own world looked past, and asks the devotee to bow there too. Notice that word, slowly. This isn't a crash course. It's a lifetime of small handings-over, one task at a time. Then the dialogue ends. Krishna sends Uddhava to Badari, a hermitage in the mountains, to live what he has heard. And Uddhava, who began this whole teaching by begging to go along with Krishna, goes where he's sent instead. The Uddhava Gita closes right there: with a student walking away from his teacher, carrying the work. Tomorrow the track turns to the word for that kind of carrying.
screen: `DO ALL YOUR WORK FOR ME, SLOWLY.` · `SEE ME IN EVERY BEING.` · `BOW EVEN WHERE OTHERS PASS BY.` · `UDDHAVA GOES WHERE HE'S SENT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hand over one task, slowly. Settle, and breathe. Choose one small piece of work waiting for you today. Picture doing it from start to finish at an unhurried pace. Then picture giving it away before you even begin. If you pray, you can offer it to the One you pray to. If you don't, you can offer it to the person it will serve. Let the breath stay slow. No rush, not even here. The bell holds the time.
Karma. At the close of the Uddhava Gita: all your work, done for the one you love, slowly, little by little. Today's word.
Your line: karma, the Bhagavata's Uddhava Gita. Today, do one task more slowly than you need to, and know who it's for. Day one thousand two hundred seven.

howItsDone: Vaishnava Hindus speak of offering their daily work to Krishna, and the eleventh book of the Bhagavata, where Krishna tells Uddhava to do all his work for his sake and to see him in every being, is one of the texts they draw on.

fork.setup: you're Uddhava. you've heard a long teaching, and you tell Krishna honestly it's too hard. what does he give you?
options: a stricter discipline to master the mind.
permission to give the whole thing up.
a simpler way: do all your work for him, slowly.
fork.reveal: Krishna answers with something simple: do all your work for his sake, remembering him, little by little.

original.note: Sanskrit: the name of Krishna's friend and questioner, for whom the Uddhava Gita is named.

trapdoor: what you thought: the path of action means doing more.
what it means: at its close, the Uddhava Gita asks for the same work, done for him, slowly, with him seen in every being.
what a scholar hears: Bhagavata Purana 11.29, the simpler means given after Uddhava calls the yoga hard, and the chapter's end, where Uddhava departs for Badarikashrama.
recall: a warrior, and a daughter coming home
the year just walked and kept

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 11.29.1–3 (Uddhava says the yoga is hard for those who cannot master the mind)
Bhagavata Purana 11.29.9 (do all actions for his sake, remembering him, little by little)
Bhagavata Purana 11.29.12–16 (see him in all beings, within and without, like the sky; bow to all, even dog, outcaste, cow and donkey, disregarding the laughter of one's own people)
Bhagavata Purana 11.29.40–47 (Krishna sends Uddhava to Badarikashrama; Uddhava departs)

notes: Last day of the Uddhava Gita strand; tomorrow begins 'seva as vocation'. Confirm that 11.29 is the close of the dialogue as commonly reckoned.
'Slowly, little by little' renders 'shanakaih' in 11.29.9 as the writer recalls it; confirm the Sanskrit and the rendering.
Uddhava's 'hard for people like us' is a paraphrase of 11.29.1–3 ('in effect'); confirm.

11.29.16 lists dog, chandala, cow and donkey; the script renders chandala as 'the person your society pushes to the edges' and notes the text names those its world looked past. A Keeper should check this framing on caste.
Verse range for Uddhava's departure to Badarikashrama is approximate; confirm.

Editor pass: 'the week on the path of action closes' became 'the Uddhava Gita closes', since the week runs on to day 1208. Day 1206's practice was changed so this day's handing-over practice is no longer repeated.
